name: preentered-two-request-fifo
scheduler_credit: Reuses baseline T031 pre-entered distinct-owner queue scaffolding. The scheduler is not a new case/mechanism and earns zero additional credit.
entry: One serial external GET /case/<id>. The frontend creates one random fresh CASE root, then performs setup, left/right cohort, finish.
placement_requirements: Use the reviewed exact direct celld executable built from the pinned recovered source; no workerd, hybrid, Node, mocked state, or in-memory SQLite stand-in.
AccountingCase is a real SQLite-backed Durable Object exported by this deployment and bound as CASE in wrangler.jsonc.

The two real ordinary DO.fetch invocations address the same object ID and stable activation. They must pre-enter distinct incoming request contexts on its actual owner before the left transaction closes the input gate.
No cross-machine distribution is claimed or required. Keep this one recipient on one stable owner; no owner migration, draining lease, process restart or fault injection belongs to this schedule.

An independent supervisor must correlate the generated rootName/objectId and activation receipts with actual direct-celld process, deployment binding and store ownership. Fixture UUIDs do not establish engine or placement provenance.
A fresh private deployment/store and fresh randomly named root are mandatory. Do not aim these fixtures at a production or shared user root.

gates.witness: setup READY, matching objectId/activation, empty KV and no application SQL tables
gates.placement: separate setup fetch finishes before cohort begins
per-activation local Promise barrier, both incoming handlers active before any trace transaction
left case body reaches its literal c.pause() inside real storage.transaction after the case-specific mutation
right request already entered; it issues real storage.transaction and then resolves the local queue notification without awaiting its result
left wait resolves only on right's issued call; right must not enter before release

gates.witness: both transaction promises and both handler responses settled
gates.placement: frontend Promise.allSettled plus recipient active/pending-transaction/timer counters

gates.witness: case fixed oracle, schedule exact relative order, cleanup COMPLETE
gates.placement: separate finish fetch after cohort settlement

cleanup: Native SQL rows are drained immediately through public cursor.next with a 64-row cap; cursor references are held only inside the activation for bounded final cleanup.
Both handler responses must settle; recipient active handlers, active callbacks, pending transaction promises, and local gate timers must all be zero before data cleanup.
A missing gate is BLOCKED_SCHEDULE. An unsettled cohort/deadline is BLOCKED_UNSETTLED with EXTERNAL_REAP_REQUIRED. No timeout or omitted schedule may count as a successful case.
deleteAll runs only on this fresh correlated owned root; verify public KV empty and user SQL schema absent. A final bounded drain/cleanup failure remains non-passing.

Timers cannot interrupt wedged native code. Independent supervisor must enforce process/RSS deadlines and reap only its owned processes/store, record teardown, and stop rather than silently enlarge limits.
acceptance: HTTP 200 and outer/finished ASSERTIONS_SATISFIED; READY setup; both SETTLED role-correlated receipts; one matching activation/objectId throughout; all nonempty assertions true; complete schedule; cleanup COMPLETE; independent exact executable/source/placement/fresh-store/limit/teardown evidence. No self-issued fixture status is a runtime PASS without these external witnesses.
